authored.objective: sv2-syntax parses a lossless CST for packages, imports, aliases, owned annotations (comment, doc, rep) in relationship bodies, part definitions, seven usages with all five feature specializations, AND the expression operator core: 106 of 558 productions. The reference grammar is DERIVED IN FULL through the six-phase pipeline and FROZEN at sha256 0b9abe64f1f3ce2b: 554 of 554 live units verified, none pending and none in conflict, in both languages. The derived grammar's oracle parses every one of the 311 corpus files and catches all 37 negatives, leaking none.
authored.next_step: THE POSTFIX LAYER of KerML 8.2.5.8.2, in Parser::primary_expression in crates/sv2-syntax/src/parser.rs. The operator core reads all fifteen precedence tiers and stops at the base expression; primary_expression currently dispatches NullExpression, SequenceExpression, LiteralExpression and FeatureReferenceExpression and nothing else. Turn it into a postfix LOOP over the base expression, because BracketExpression, IndexExpression, FeatureChainExpression, SelectExpression, CollectExpression and FunctionOperationExpression are all written left-recursive in the frozen reference (reference.ebnf lines 68, 85, 171, 218, 236, 445) and so are left-associative BY CONSTRUCTION -- unlike the fifteen tiers, this layer needs no table. Build each node retroactively with Parser::start_node_at and Parser::wrap_at at a checkpoint taken before the base expression, exactly as Parser::infix_tail already does. START WITH FeatureChainExpression ('.') and BracketExpression ('['), and do BracketExpression's disambiguation first because it is the one hard part: '[' after a declared feature name is a MultiplicityPart (SysML 8.2.2.6.6, IMPLEMENTED, Parser::multiplicity_part) and '[' after an expression operand is a BracketExpression (the quantity form, 297 corpus hits such as `1200 [kg]` and the hard case `(hubDiameter + 2 * tire.height) [mm]` at validation/15-Properties-Values-Expressions/15_03-Value Expression.sysml line 15). Those two are the SAME TOKEN in different roles and the parser must not confuse them; tests/rejection/bracket-expression-is-not-implemented.sysml states the distinction and is the case to remove when it lands, alongside feature-chain-expression-is-not-implemented.sysml. Do NOT start with SelectExpression, CollectExpression or FunctionOperationExpression's body form: all three take a BodyArgumentMember, which reaches BodyExpression -> ExpressionBody, and in SysML that reads CalculationBody, which is most of the language.

pending_decisions.question: RESOLVED. regen_state.py recorded `git log --oneline -8` in the generated block and --check compared it, which has no fixed point: the commit carrying state.json cannot record its own hash, and amending only moves it. The gate was therefore red after every commit, for ever. Fixed by naming the compared measurements explicitly — COMPARED = (coverage, tests, pins) — and a pure is_stale() over them, with four tests including the one that says a new commit is not staleness. `commits` is still measured and written for whoever reads the block at session start; it is simply not evidence. Nothing else read it: not state_report.py, not the schema's required list. NOT weakened: coverage, tests and pins are still compared exactly as before, so an un-regenerated block after real work still fails.

Two pipeline defects had to be fixed first (plan enumerated the Xtext inventory; freeze check went red on the first derived unit); both are fixed and tested.

RESOLVED. A unit no longer embeds its clause: it keeps the citation and a sha256 of the clause text, and grammar_next.py joins the text from the local export at read time. How is '[' disambiguated between MultiplicityPart and BracketExpression? Both are implemented-or-planned in the same grammar and the token is identical. The working hypothesis is positional -- a '[' reached from UsageDeclaration's FeatureSpecializationPart is a multiplicity, a '[' reached from an expression operand is a BracketExpression -- which is what the current code already does by construction, since multiplicity_part is only called from feature_specialization_part. Confirm that holds for every corpus shape before BracketExpression lands, in particular where a value part's expression is followed by a unit: `attribute m = 1200 [kg];` reaches the '[' from the expression side with a MultiplicityPart already consumed on the declaration side.
blocks: BracketExpression, IndexExpression, and the 297 corpus files that write a bracketed unit

pending_decisions.question: Is MAX_DEPTH = 400 in crates/sv2-syntax/src/parser.rs the right recursion limit, and should it be configurable? It was introduced this session because the recursive expression parser OVERFLOWED THE STACK, which aborts the process and so is strictly worse than the panic invariant 3 forbids. Measured thresholds before the guard: unary operators between 2000 and 5000 levels, parenthesised expressions and nested bodies between 5000 and 10000. Note the nested-body path had this flaw ALREADY -- it is not new with the expression layer. 400 is far past anything a person writes, but it is a number nobody derived from a source, and it changes what the parser accepts.

log.summary: Closed the SysML grammar and froze the reference. 473 to 554 of 554 live units verified, none pending and none in conflict; frozen at sha256 0b9abe64f1f3ce2b, 554 productions, ledger entry 1. The oracle went from 155 to all 311 corpus files accepted, still catching all 37 negatives with none leaked. Four filed specification defects repaired and recorded, each issue page fetched and read: SYSML21-408 and -624 (both in SendNode's single line), -400 (ControlNodePrefix) and -401 (TriggerExpression). ForVariableDeclarationMember adjudicated, which left SysML with no unreachable production. The oracle's state guard was re-derived from a measurement: ~143 items per token scaling linearly, so the 400_000 absolute cap was mis-calibrated rather than the grammar ambiguous, and it is now a per-token budget with four tests. Also declared sv2-ast, sv2-hir and sv2-resolve as stub crates, and proposed ADR-0016 and ADR-0017.

Implemented the expression operator core: OwnedExpression by precedence climbing over the fifteen tiers of KerML 8.2.5.8.1 table 6, plus MultiplicityPart, ValuePart and ElementFilterMember, which it unblocked. Coverage 57 to 106 of 558; negative cases 49 to 65. Precedence is NOT in the grammar and cannot be -- note 2 of that clause says so -- so the parser reads docs/operator-precedence.toml, and a test diffs that file against the parser's INFIX table both ways so neither can be edited alone; deviations.json had already recorded the decision under BinaryOperatorExpression as spec_only/follow_spec. Found and fixed a defect this introduced: deep nesting overflowed the stack, which aborts rather than panics and so breaks invariant 3; added MAX_DEPTH and a round-trip test at 50000 levels for parentheses, unary operators and nested bodies. spec-conformance-reviewer returned one blocking finding, all fixed: the FeatureSpecializationPart comment quoted the Pilot's '( -> FeatureSpecialization )+' syntactic predicate as though it were KerML 8.2.4.3.1, and that '->' is in neither specification's BNF. Also committed a draft docs/CRATES.md and the author's spelling corrections to README.md and NOTICE.md.
